facts.fact: Kirri's silver anklet had its bells cut off; she never took it off, even to bathe. She swore to send it in a fish-basket as a sign once she had her boat.
facts.why: needed because the beat requires Kirri's anklet sign and its non-arrival; it matches the kennel anklet in ch 26.

facts.fact: Ammu has written eleven times to Kirri's address and Chathu answers only 'Kirri is where she wished to be, child.'
facts.why: needed because it shows Ammu's fear and plants C09.

facts.fact: Seven wells is a pebble-tossing game on a plank with seven hollows; a pebble counts only if it strikes the hollow's wall and then drops, and rivals' stones may be flicked out. Cheats get a ladle rap on the knuckles.
facts.why: needed because the beat names the game and requires cheating.

facts.fact: Devan played seven wells once at eight and Asha beat him, which he says was by cheating.
facts.why: needed because it gives the game emotional weight and ties to Asha.

facts.fact: Neela counts sixteen nights left on the day of chapter 18, with the meeting at the stone by day and the game that evening.
facts.why: needed because it continues the countdown from ch 17.

facts.fact: Kannan gives Neela a white pebble from the game to keep.
facts.why: needed as a small object for the closing beat.
